question.text: What is the significance of the record date for IDCW (dividend) payment in mutual funds?

answer.text: Investors who hold units on the record date are eligible to receive the IDCW payment
It is the date when the IDCW amount is decided by SEBI
It is the last date to invest in the scheme
It is the date when the fund manager rebalances the portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: The record date is the cut-off date that a mutual fund uses to fix the list of unit-holders eligible for an IDCW (Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal) payout. Investors whose names appear on the register as unit-holders on the record date receive the IDCW for that distribution; investors who purchase units after the record date do not, even though they own units when the payout is actually made. The Trap: "The date when the IDCW amount is decided by SEBI" is wrong — SEBI does not set IDCW amounts; the AMC's trustees declare distributions. "Last date to invest in the scheme" describes scheme closure or NFO cut-off, not record date. "Date when the fund manager rebalances the portfolio" confuses an unrelated portfolio-management activity with a distribution-administration date. Note: The explicit definition of record-date eligibility for IDCW (that investors holding units on the record date are eligible) is not stated on the cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (125, 133, 169, 171); those pages discuss IDCW entitlement by option and dividend transfer after the record date. The framing above reflects general industry and regulatory practice for IDCW distributions.
